Results and proofs

Domains and Constructions of Beilinson–Bloch Height Pairings

Complete and partial cases, with their proof dependencies

23 November 2026

Abstract

We organize the geometric domains of zero-curvature Green forms and normalized Beilinson–Bloch height pairings. Under explicit actual-form, numerical and reciprocity hypotheses, Chow covariance turns decompositions and model corrections into constructions on the exact support complement of a prescribed cycle. The resulting domains include products of arbitrary curves and surfaces, their specified motivic summands, Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces, and the surface-moduli motives furnished by Bülles. Other applications use low-dimensional diagonal support, Chow niveau, flat fibrations, and semistable models. We give the precise complementary-degree conditions for global heights, construct Chow identities for separated hypersurfaces and cyclic covers, and record the field and cover degrees in the comparison with classical abelian heights. The geometric proofs are given in full; the separately supplied analytic and model statements are identified at each use.

For complete intersections cut out by global functions, Mihatsch constructs such forms explicitly [25, Theorem 5.5]. The general projective problem requires a global compatibility condition. The companion obstruction theory now constructs a Chow-invariant actual Bott–Chern class and a curved pair for every prescribed cycle [1, Theorem 1.1]. Vanishing of this obstruction allows one to correct a curved Green form for the original cycle by a global ordinary form. The algebraic question is therefore to identify Chow sources on which this obstruction vanishes.

The present paper develops this question through Chow decompositions, semistable models, and explicit geometric constructions. Its analytic foundation is stated in Section 2: the cycle obstruction is established, while the numerical-model, Chow-covariance and height premises are retained at their points of use. We first describe the abelian transfer, which also provides a classical formula for the height. The required algebraic datum is literal. Theorem 1.5 (Geometric domains). Assume the analytic hypotheses of Section 2 and the model inputs specified in the cited sections. Let K/QpK/\mathbb Q_pK/Qp​ be finite. Each of the following smooth projective geometrically integral varieties has property V\mathsf VV.

In particular this includes products of point Hilbert schemes of arbitrary surfaces with curves and the allowed coefficient TTT, as well as the surface-moduli motives specified in Section 5.

For every specified geometrically homologically trivial cycle, property V\mathsf VV supplies a form satisfying (1.1) on its exact support complement. For a number-field variety to which one of these criteria applies at every finite completion, the normalized pairing has a full height domain.

The proofs of (i), (ii)–(iii), and (iv) occupy Section 4, Section 5, and Section 6–Section 11, respectively. The global assertion follows from Lemma 4.2. Geometric constructions can be base changed to all completions; a reduction condition on TTT is imposed separately at each finite place.

The distinction between a local degree range and a global height range is useful even when all degrees are not covered. If S⊆{1,…,n}S\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}S⊆{1,…,n} is the set of local degrees established at every finite place, then the full height pairs occur in S∩(n+1−S). S\cap(n+1-S).S∩(n+1−S).(1.8) For example, small diagonal support gives local degrees r≤2r\leq2r≤2 or r≥n−2r\geq n-2r≥n−2; for n≥6n\geq6n≥6 the corresponding full height degrees are r≤2r\leq2r≤2 or r≥n−1r\geq n-1r≥n−1.

On an arbitrary smooth projective variety, the same formalism applies to subgroups. In particular algebraically trivial cycles lie in the local obstruction kernel in every degree. This gives the pairing on the two algebraically trivial groups described in Section 12.

1.2. Proof strategy and relation to earlier work

The local transfer has three steps. First, Künnemann’s exact complex on a strictly semistable abelian model produces a cycle extension whose restriction to every special-fiber component is homologically trivial. The companion numerical criterion then annihilates the actual obstruction. Second, the diagonal identity expresses an original Chow class as a sum of images of homologically trivial abelian classes. Chow-kernel covariance transfers their vanishing and the full finite degree descends it to KKK. Third, the original curved Green pair is corrected on XXX itself. This last step retains the original support.

For the separated-variable families, a single join step has source Bl⁡C(A×B)\operatorname{Bl}_C(A\times B)BlC​(A×B) with a smooth codimension-two center CCC. Both the ambient product and the center have lower-complexity Chow factorizations. The exact blowup identity and the degree retraction therefore give a recursive factorization for the target. For cyclic covers, the additional map from an ordinary hypersurface is finite flat everywhere, of rank mmm. Its full rank is the factor in the Chow identity and in the height formula.

The geometry of abelian-type motives and the classical abelian height are inputs to this argument. Künnemann’s height already has correspondence functoriality and finite-extension compatibility [26, §1]. Our height formula records its realization by the companion ordinary-form theory and the precise scalar in the explicit Chow constructions. The companion references in Section 2 separate this analytic input from the algebraic arguments proved here.

After the analytic input and abelian transfer, we treat the endpoint degrees, small diagonal support, products, Chow niveau, and flat fibrations. The explicit Chow identities then give separated hypersurfaces and cyclic covers. The final sections discuss model criteria, global families, and the normalized height formulas.

2.2. Numerical witnesses and Chow covariance

We state the numerical input in the finite constant-field case used in this paper. A pure operational representative of a codimension-rrr cycle on a regular model means a rational virtual vector bundle whose Chern character has that cycle in degree rrr and vanishes in all other degrees. Such a representative is part of the companion construction.

Proposition 4.3 (Endpoint input). For a smooth projective nnn-fold over the original KKK, geometric homological divisors, zero-cycles and one-cycles have zero obstruction. Thus V(X)\mathsf V(X)V(X) holds if n≤3n\leq3n≤3.

The divisor and zero-cycle assertions are the endpoint results in [12]. For one-cycles, the precise input is the regular-model curve correction followed by dominant obstruction descent, also recorded there. Its proof proceeds as follows. Choose a projective strictly semistable alteration V→XV\to XV→X, over a finite constant extension, of the same dimension as XXX. The pullback of a homologically trivial one-cycle remains a one-cycle. This uses the full degree of the alteration and leaves the final curved-pair correction on XXX.

4.3. Projective bundles and dominant images

For a projective dominant morphism f:V→Xf:V\to Xf:V→X with relative dimension eee, choose a relatively ample class aaa whose top degree on the generic fiber is d>0d>0d>0. Corollary 4.9. A geometrically uniruled smooth projective fourfold has V\mathsf VV. So does any smooth projective dominant morphism image of a projective-bundle tower over a variety of dimension at most three, or over one of these uniruled fourfolds.

Proof. After a finite extension, a uniruled fourfold is dominated rationally by B×P1B\times\mathbb P^1B×P1 for a smooth projective threefold BBB. Resolve this map in characteristic zero by smooth blowups of the four-dimensional source. Every nontrivial center has dimension at most two, hence has V\mathsf VV. The source and its resolution have V\mathsf VV by Proposition 4.8. The resolved dominant morphism transfers it to XXX. The remaining assertions follow successively from projective bundle and dominant-morphism transfer. ◻

The proof is [13, model splitting theorem], whose actual deletion and residual-core constructions are included in the proof dossier. The essential structure is as follows. Each component is a tower of blowups of closed strata in the full reduced boundary of a product of smooth curve and surface components. For a subset III of the surface indices, coordinate deletion gives an actual proper birational map fI:Di⟶(∏j∈IXj,ij)×W−I,i−I, f_I:D_{\boldsymbol i}\longrightarrow \left(\prod_{j\in I}X_{j,i_j}\right)\times W_{-I,\boldsymbol i_{-I}},fI​:Di​⟶​j∈I∏​Xj,ij​​​×W−I,i−I​​,(5.2) where W−IW_{-I}W−I​ is the staircase component of the remaining factors. Theorem 5.2 (Arbitrary curve and surface products). Let X1,…,Xm/KX_1,\ldots,X_m/KX1​,…,Xm​/K be arbitrary smooth projective geometrically integral curves or surfaces. Let T/KT/KT/K be smooth projective geometrically integral with potentially good projective reduction. Then X=T×∏a=1mXaX=T\times\prod_{a=1}^mX_aX=T×a=1∏m​Xa​ has V\mathsf VV. The assertion holds over every finite extension of KKK for every newly specified geometrically homologically trivial cycle there. Empty products and a point as coefficient are permitted.

Proof. After a common finite extension choose projective strictly semistable alterations of the low-dimensional factors and a smooth projective model of TTT. Semistable repair after any intermediate ramified extension is part of the ordered-model construction in [13]. Apply Proposition 5.1 to the resulting witness. Weight–monodromy for curves and surfaces, the purity of the good coefficient, and Künneth give the odd-weight condition in the companion model criterion. Equations (5.3) and (5.4) supply its two exactness conditions. The pulled-back obstruction therefore vanishes. Dominant and finite-degree descent give zero obstruction over KKK; the original curved pair gives the requested form.

For an arbitrary finite K′/KK'/KK′/K, the factors still have the same dimensions and the coefficient remains potentially good. Reapply the construction over K′K'K′ to its newly specified cycle. This proves the assertion for new classes, as well as for pullbacks of old ones. ◻

Over a number field, the curves and surfaces are unrestricted. If a coefficient TTT is present, it is required to have potentially good projective reduction at every finite place. Applying Theorem 5.2 at all completions and using Lemma 4.2 gives the full height in every complementary degree, also after every finite number-field extension.

5.2. Abelian factors and the surface-generated Chow domain

Lemma 5.3. Over a characteristic-zero field, an abelian variety becomes a rational Chow-motive retract of a product of curves after a finite extension.

Proof. For an abelian variety of dimension g≥2g\geq2g≥2, choose a smooth complete-intersection curve and a point c0c_0c0​ on it after a finite extension. Translate by −c0-c_0−c0​ and call the resulting pointed curve CCC; choose the complete intersection so that C−CC-CC−C generates AAA. The addition map Cg→AC^g\to ACg→A is dominant. Indeed, the successive sums of CCC increase in dimension until they fill AAA: stabilization at a proper subvariety would make that subvariety stable under the group generated by CCC. Since source and target have dimension ggg, the map is generically finite, of some degree d>0d>0d>0. Its graph satisfies f∗f∗=dΔAf_*f^*=d\Delta_Af∗​f∗=dΔA​, and d−1f∗d^{-1}f_*d−1f∗​ is a Chow retraction. Dimension one is immediate; dimension zero gives the unit motive. ◻

Corollary 5.4. Suppose that after a finite extension the rational Chow motive of XXX is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of Tate twists of products of curves and surfaces. Then V(X)\mathsf V(X)V(X) holds. It also holds for T×XT\times XT×X with a potentially good projective coefficient. These conclusions include products with arbitrary abelian factors.

Proof. Choose the inclusion and retraction correspondences. Their composites sum to the diagonal. Tensor with the coefficient’s diagonal when needed, apply Theorem 5.2 to each intermediate variety, and use Lemma 4.1. An abelian factor may first be replaced by its curve-product retraction from Lemma 5.3. ◻

5.4. Finite specialization of Chow certificates

Lemma 5.6. Let X/kX/kX/k be smooth projective in characteristic zero. Suppose that over a field extension Ω/k\Omega/kΩ/k its diagonal factors in rational Chow through finitely many products of smooth projective curves and surfaces. Then such a factorization exists over a finite extension E/kE/kE/k, with auxiliary curves and surfaces allowed to change.

Proof. Choose cycle representatives for the correspondences and finitely many principal divisors witnessing the diagonal equality. All these data, together with the auxiliary varieties and their projective embeddings, descend to a field finitely generated over kkk. Spread them over a smooth integral finite-type kkk-scheme BBB. Shrink BBB so that the auxiliary families are smooth projective with geometrically integral fibers, the cycles have their expected codimensions, and the relative Chow equality holds. The last step follows either by spreading its principal-divisor certificate or by the direct-limit description of Chow groups over the function field.

Choose a closed point b∈Bb\in Bb∈B. Its residue field EEE is finite over kkk. Since BBB is smooth, refined pullback to bbb commutes with the smooth pullbacks, proper projections and diagonal intersections which define correspondence composition. The constant family X×BX\times BX×B specializes to XEX_EXE​, while the auxiliary families specialize to smooth curves and surfaces. Thus the diagonal certificate specializes with all its degree shifts. ◻

Theorem 5.7 (Complex certificates and surface moduli). Let X/FX/FX/F be smooth projective over a number field. If for one complex embedding h(XC)h(X_\mathbb C)h(XC​) retracts through products of curves and surfaces in rational Chow motives, then XXX has a full height domain, also after every finite number-field extension. In particular this holds if XCX_\mathbb CXC​ is a smooth projective moduli space appearing in Bülles’s theorem: Gieseker-stable twisted sheaves, or stable objects for a generic stability condition, on a complex projective K3 or abelian surface. Finite products of these spaces and the varieties in Theorem 5.5 are allowed, with an everywhere potentially good projective coefficient.

Proof. By Lemma 5.6, a finite extension E/FE/FE/F carries an actual diagonal certificate of the required kind. Complete it at a place above each finite place of FFF and apply Corollary 5.4; full-degree descent gives the original local kernel vanishing. The same construction over a compositum treats every new cycle after finite extension. Apply Lemma 4.2.

For the moduli spaces, [3, Theorem 0.1] supplies precisely an actual rational Chow retraction through powers of the underlying surface. The first assertion applies. For products, tensor the certificates; the intermediate varieties remain products of curves and surfaces. The surface’s finite-dimensionality is not an assumption of the cited retraction theorem. ◻

7. Actual Chow identities

For the algebraic arguments, let kkk be any characteristic-zero field. Write Ak(V)\mathcal A_k(V)Ak​(V) for a diagonal factorization of VVV through abelian varieties over kkk itself, in the sense of (1.2) with L=kL=kL=k. Smooth disconnected varieties are interpreted by the direct sum of their components.

Lemma 7.1. The property Ak\mathcal A_kAk​ is stable under finite products, finite disjoint unions of pure-dimensional components, isomorphisms and base extension. A pointed smooth projective geometrically integral curve has this property.

Proof. For products, take exterior products of the two sets of correspondences, with the factors ordered as source and target. Composition commutes with exterior products, so ΔV×W=ΔV⊠ΔW=∑j,l(vj⊠vl)∘(uj⊠ul).\Delta_{V\times W}=\Delta_V\boxtimes\Delta_W =\sum_{j,l}(v_j\boxtimes v_l)\circ(u_j\boxtimes u_l).ΔV×W​=ΔV​⊠ΔW​=j,l∑​(vj​⊠vl​)∘(uj​⊠ul​). The intermediate variety Aj×AlA_j\times A_lAj​×Al​ is abelian. This equality is in the Chow group of the product with itself. Disjoint unions and isomorphisms follow by inserting component maps and by conjugating with graphs; flat field extension preserves the identity.

For a pointed curve CCC, use h(C)=1⊕h1(C)⊕Lh(C)=\mathbf1\oplus h^1(C)\oplus\mathbb Lh(C)=1⊕h1(C)⊕L and the identification of h1(C)h^1(C)h1(C) with the corresponding summand of h(J(C))h(J(C))h(J(C)). These are Chow-motive decompositions [30, §3.2, Proposition 4.5 and Theorems 5.2–5.3]. Their inclusion and retraction maps, with the Tate terms through Spec⁡k\operatorname{Spec}kSpeck, give the required identity. ◻

8. Separated binary hypersurfaces

Allow first 2b+a≥22b+a\ge22b+a≥2 in (1.3), so that zero-dimensional factors can occur in an induction. These factors are finite étale. For every binary block, Euler’s identity shows that simultaneous vanishing of its derivatives at a nonzero vector would give a multiple projective root. A nonzero unary term has nonvanishing derivative away from zero in characteristic zero. The full gradient therefore vanishes only at the affine origin. The hypersurface is smooth; when its dimension is positive, connectedness of a projective hypersurface makes it geometrically integral.

9. Split cubics and finite Chow descent

Laterveer proves that the cubic varieties (1.4) over C\mathbb CC have Chow motives of abelian type [28, Theorem 5]. This is a conclusion about rational equivalence, and gives a retract of a finite sum of Tate twists of abelian motives. We need its finite field of definition, including the rational equivalences in the retraction.

Lemma 9.1. Let k0/Qk_0/\mathbb Qk0​/Q be finitely generated, let V0/k0V_0/k_0V0​/k0​ be smooth projective, and fix an embedding k0↪Ck_0\hookrightarrow\mathbb Ck0​↪C. If h(V0,C)h(V_{0,\mathbb C})h(V0,C​) is of abelian type, then an actual abelian Chow retraction of V0V_0V0​ is defined over a finite extension k1/k0k_1/k_0k1​/k0​. For every embedding k0↪kk_0\hookrightarrow kk0​↪k into a characteristic-zero field, it therefore exists over a finite extension of kkk.

Proof. Vial’s descent theorem [29, Theorem 1 and §1.1] applies to the extension kˉ0⊂C\bar k_0\subset\mathbb Ckˉ0​⊂C. It shows that h(V0,kˉ0)h(V_{0,\bar k_0})h(V0,kˉ0​​) is of abelian type. By the definition of this category, it is a retract of a finite sum of Tate twists of motives of abelian varieties: tensor products remain abelian motives, and duality is absorbed by a Tate twist. Thus there are finitely many correspondences satisfying the diagonal identity over kˉ0\bar k_0kˉ0​.

The varieties, group laws, cycles, and rational equivalences in that identity are all defined by finitely many coefficients. After clearing rational denominators, each rational equivalence is a finite sum of divisors of rational functions on integral subvarieties. These data descend to one finite subextension k1/k0k_1/k_0k1​/k0​. Equivalently, the finitely many equalities in the Chow groups hold at a finite stage of their directed limit over kˉ0\bar k_0kˉ0​.

Extend k0↪kk_0\hookrightarrow kk0​↪k to k1↪kˉk_1\hookrightarrow\bar kk1​↪kˉ. Then L=kk1L=kk_1L=kk1​ is finite over kkk, and flat base change carries the same Chow identity to LLL. ◻

9.1. Application to the block family

For a cubic over kkk as in (1.4), put its coefficients in a finitely generated subfield k0⊂kk_0\subset kk0​⊂k. The smoothness assumptions descend and remain true after embedding k0k_0k0​ into C\mathbb CC. Laterveer’s theorem applies there, and Lemma 9.1 gives the required finite Chow factorization over kkk. Tensoring the factorizations deals with products; transporting them through an actual isomorphism deals with finite forms. This proves part (ii) of Theorem 1.3.

For example, two arbitrary smooth cubic threefold blocks followed by a smooth binary cubic give a cubic tenfold in P11\mathbb P^{11}P11. Replacing the binary block by a smooth four-variable cubic gives a cubic twelvefold in P13\mathbb P^{13}P13. Their central cycle codimensions are 555 and 666. The two five-variable blocks need not themselves separate into binary terms.

11. Model criteria and arithmetic families

11.1. Numerical corrections on a semistable witness

The numerical-model criterion of Hypothesis 2.2 is often applied through a projective dominant witness. In the general companion formulation [12], the witness carries a rational virtual bundle whose generic degree-rrr Chern character is the pulled-back class and whose degree on every vertical rrr-dimensional subvariety is zero. The native model-Chern detector then gives zero obstruction upstairs, and dominant detection gives zero obstruction downstairs. This formulation permits a witness of positive relative dimension as well as a generically finite one.

We record three ways of producing this numerical correction. The model calculations and their supporting residue sequences are given in [16]; all model conditions below refer to supplied projective models.

Such a subspace pairs globally with the admitted complementary group.

11.2. Ordinary quadratic reduction

Theorem 11.4 (Companion ordinary-reduction theorem). Let K/QpK/\mathbb Q_pK/Qp​ be finite for any prime ppp, and let X/KX/KX/K be smooth projective geometrically integral of dimension at least three. Suppose XXX has an integral flat projective model whose geometric special fiber is integral and smooth apart from finitely many ordinary quadratic points, meaning that their projectivized geometric tangent cones are smooth quadrics. Then V(X)\mathsf V(X)V(X) holds. The same conclusion holds if such a smooth projective dominant witness is supplied after a finite extension. The theorem reapplies to all new cycles over every finite valued extension.

Proof. In odd residue characteristic the normal-form and successive reduced-point blowup calculation of [17] produces a regular reduced quadric forest after finite extension. Its numerical corrections are compatible with the incidence maps. The all-characteristic quadric-forest theorem in the same source handles odd-dimensional ordinary quadratic models at residue two.

For even n≥4n\geq4n≥4 at residue two, use the henselian normal form of [10, Lemma 4(ii)]. A common finite extension splits all the finitely many node polynomials. Translating each by an integral root gives an actual pointed étale local equation P(x1,…,xn)+z2+ϵϖqz=0,q≥1,ϵ∈R×,P(x_1,\ldots,x_n)+z^2+\epsilon\varpi^qz=0, \qquad q\geq1,\quad\epsilon\in R^\times,P(x1​,…,xn​)+z2+ϵϖqz=0,q≥1,ϵ∈R×, with unimodular polar form for PPP, where RRR is the auxiliary field’s valuation ring and ϖ\varpiϖ its uniformizer. The common étale charts and exact saturated blowup calculations are proved in [17, common étale neighborhoods and native degenerate-node chains]. Each reduced-point blowup decreases qqq by one. After exactly qqq blowups the exceptional chain consists of q−1q-1q−1 copies of PE(OE⊕OE(−1))\mathbb P_E(\mathcal O_E\oplus\mathcal O_E(-1))PE​(OE​⊕OE​(−1)) and a terminal smooth quadric, where E=(P‾(X)+Z2=0)⊂Pn,T=(P‾(X)+Z2+ϵ‾ZS=0)⊂Pn+1.E=(\overline P(X)+Z^2=0)\subset\mathbb P^n, \qquad T=(\overline P(X)+Z^2+\overline\epsilon ZS=0) \subset\mathbb P^{n+1}.E=(P(X)+Z2=0)⊂Pn,T=(P(X)+Z2+ϵZS=0)⊂Pn+1. All double strata are the smooth odd-dimensional quadric EEE; all multiplicities are one and the intermediate sections are disjoint. The same quadric-forest numerical criterion now applies.

In every case numerical witness descent uses the complete common field degree, and the original curved pair gives the form on the specified support complement. The dominant-witness version follows from the same detector. After a finite valued extension the ordinary geometric special points persist, with possibly larger finite orders; apply the construction anew to every new cycle. ◻

Over a number field, good reduction or the ordinary alternative at every finite completion, also on the stated dominant witnesses, gives the full height pairing. Local auxiliary extensions are descended before this global construction and need not come from one fixed global extension.

11.3. Tate and abelian-type strata

Theorem 11.5 (Companion all-strata criterion). Let Y,T/KY,T/KY,T/K be smooth projective geometrically integral. Suppose YYY has a supplied regular projective reduced strictly semistable model whose every connected closed geometric stratum has a rational Chow motive of abelian type after finite constants. Assume weight–monodromy for YYY in every degree and every invertible coefficient prime. If TTT has potentially good projective reduction, then T×YT\times YT×Y has V\mathsf VV, also for all new cycles after every finite valued extension.

Proof. The ramified all-strata theorem in [18] preserves the stated Chow-motive condition on a projective semistable repair. Its toroidal calculation expresses new strata through blowups of old boundary strata and projective bundles over them. For a closed-boundary blowup the property holds in both directions; this permits the toroidal factorization steps. The character lattice of a new stratum is primitive, and its calculation retains the actual line-bundle transition functions.

For a new cycle over L/KL/KL/K, pass to a finite extension where TTT is good and the strata split. On one abelian carrier, numerical semisimplicity and its comparison prime supply an algebraic cohomological inner inverse to the boundary incidence. Tensor it with the diagonal of the coefficient, so the inverse acts on all mixed Künneth summands. Weight–monodromy gives the odd-weight condition, while the inverse gives numerical-kernel lifting and actual-span saturation. Apply the companion model criterion and descend with the full degree. The final curved-pair correction is on the original support of the newly specified cycle. ◻

Corollary 11.6 (Drinfeld uniformization). Let XaX_aXa​ be smooth projective algebraizations of Γa\ΩKda\Gamma_a\backslash\Omega_K^{d_a}Γa​\ΩKda​​, where Γa⊂PGL⁡da+1(K)\Gamma_a\subset\operatorname{PGL}_{d_a+1}(K)Γa​⊂PGLda​+1​(K) is torsion-free, discrete and cocompact, and da≥1d_a\geq1da​≥1. Then T×∏aXaT\times\prod_aX_aT×∏a​Xa​ has V\mathsf VV for every potentially good projective coefficient TTT, also over every finite extension.

Proof. The projective semistable cover of a Drinfeld quotient has components and closed strata obtained by the successive rational-linear-subspace blowups of projective space. Their actual Chow motives are split Tate, by the blowup formula. Staircase products retain this property. Ito’s theorem [9] gives weight–monodromy, and Künneth gives it for the product. Apply Theorem 11.5 and descend the finite cover. ◻

One may also include curve or surface factors supplied with projective strict semistable models all of whose closed strata are of Chow abelian type. The resulting placewise presentations give full global heights when available at every finite completion; the factors in those local presentations may depend on the place.

Suppose a smooth projective X/KX/KX/K has, over a finite extension L/KL/KL/K, a projective dominant generically finite morphism Y→XLY\to X_LY→XL​, with YYY smooth projective geometrically integral of dimension dim⁡X\dim XdimX and carrying a regular projective reduced strictly semistable model. The cycle isomorphisms and Poincaré duality identify native numerical groups with even cohomology, compatibly with the actual incidence correspondences. 11.4. A common arithmetic construction

The dense families below use actual local models, together with an arithmetic pencil argument. We give the latter separately to specify the field and density quantifiers.

Lemma 11.8 (Congruence pencils). Let a fixed integral flat projective ambient model with geometrically integral fibers and a section system be supplied over a number ring. Suppose a finite free coefficient module surjects onto the section system and its required residue spaces. Suppose the system has a nonempty fixed-member Lefschetz-pencil open, and that one can prescribe smooth sections at a finite set of places and an established local smoothing model at distinguished places. Require the chosen equations to be nonzero on every special ambient fiber, and the generic smooth-member open to consist of geometrically integral members. After a single finite extension realizing these finite residue data, the congruence-pencil construction gives a Zariski-dense set of smooth generic members with the prescribed local models, smooth reduction at the exceptional places, and smooth or ordinary-quadratic reduction at all remaining places.

Proof. Choose a smooth reference section H0H_0H0​ and include in a finite set all rational primes below its bad reductions, its zero special sections, and residue characteristic two. Prepare the desired residue sections after finite residue extensions. A monic polynomial with separable irreducible reductions of one common degree realizes all these extensions in one number field, unramified at the chosen primes. This field is fixed from now on.

In the free coefficient module impose the finite congruences for a second section H1H_1H1​, using the square of each native maximal ideal to retain a prescribed first-order smoothing. For a distinguished rational prime ppp unramified in the starting number field, this is the modulus p2p^2p2 used in the applications. Intersect this affine congruence lattice with the fixed-H0H_0H0​ Lefschetz open. The intersection is Zariski dense. For a chosen H1H_1H1​, spread its pencil outside a finite further set of primes. At those additional primes, choose the parameter to specialize to the already smooth reference member; at the originally prepared primes choose it to preserve the chosen residue member. Chinese remainders give infinitely many parameters with these requirements. Omit the finitely many singular generic members.

Outside the spreading set, the pencil has smooth or ordinary quadratic fibers. At every exceptional prime the selected residue fiber is smooth or is the prescribed established smoothing. The nonzero residue equations are non-zero-divisors on the integral ambient fibers. The relative Cartier criterion therefore makes the resulting divisors flat over the number ring. Generic geometric integrality follows from the prescribed open. In each application, nonzero residue equations are checked at the exceptional primes by the congruences and elsewhere by independence of the two pencil sections. Finally a polynomial vanishing on all constructed members vanishes on each permitted pencil, since that pencil contains infinitely many of them. Varying H1H_1H1​ in the dense congruence open proves density in the stated section space. The finite spreading set may depend on H1H_1H1​; the fixed field does not. ◻

12.1. Algebraically trivial cycles

Write CH⁡r(X)Q,alg\operatorname{CH}^r(X)_{\mathbb Q,\mathrm{alg}}CHr(X)Q,alg​ for the rational Chow classes whose base change to an algebraic closure is algebraically equivalent to zero.

Proposition 12.1. On every smooth projective X/KX/KX/K and in every codimension, CH⁡r(X)Q,alg⊆KKr(X).\operatorname{CH}^r(X)_{\mathbb Q,\mathrm{alg}}\subseteq\mathcal K_K^r(X).CHr(X)Q,alg​⊆KKr​(X). Proof. Algebraic equivalence is generated by connected smooth projective curve families. After a finite extension, an algebraically trivial class is a finite sum of Γ∗([a]−[b]),Γ∈CH⁡r(C×X)Q,\Gamma_*([a]-[b]),\qquad \Gamma\in\operatorname{CH}^r(C\times X)_\mathbb Q,Γ∗​([a]−[b]),Γ∈CHr(C×X)Q​, with a,ba,ba,b rational over that finite extension on the smooth projective parameter curve. The constant-field interpretation of algebraic triviality is equivalently obtained by norming the finite family certificate. Apply this inclusion at every completion and then the companion height theorem. ◻

Together with the endpoint results, this also gives the full divisor–zero-cycle height on an arbitrary nnn-fold. The complete one-cycle group lies in Hn−1(X)\mathcal H^{n-1}(X)Hn−1(X) and pairs with H2(X)\mathcal H^2(X)H2(X). Whenever one of the geometric or model criteria above establishes the entire codimension-two group, this becomes the full complementary pairing.

12.2. Finite obstruction certificates

The finite-detector theorem of [23] provides, for a fixed admissible model calculation, finitely many rational period coordinates for the actual obstruction. Their vanishing is a certificate that a specified homological Chow class belongs to KKr(X)\mathcal K_K^r(X)KKr​(X). The normalized tests use ηj=1[L:K]cLTr⁡XL/XK(bj),cL=−log⁡∣ϖL∣=cK/e(L/K).\eta_j=\frac{1}{[L:K]c_L}\operatorname{Tr}^K_{X_L/X}(b_j),\qquad c_L=-\log|\varpi_L|=c_K/e(L/K).ηj​=[L:K]cL​1​TrXL​/XK​(bj​),cL​=−log∣ϖL​∣=cK​/e(L/K). Thus all model families, isotypic sectors and individually certified classes may be combined inside the same admitted group. For a number-field class one checks this membership at its finitely many relevant bad places; the good places are handled by the good-model construction. The output Green identity still has the complete actual test space in (1.1).

13. Height pairings and recursive formulas

13.1. Proof of the normalized height theorem

Let X/FX/FX/F satisfy the hypothesis of Theorem 1.4. At each finite place vvv, complete a field of definition of the Chow retraction at a place above vvv. The resulting extension of FvF_vFv​ is finite. Theorem 1.2, applied with the original absolute value of FvF_vFv​, shows that every geometric homological class has zero local obstruction. Both groups in (1.6) are therefore in the full domain of the companion height theorem.

Normalized finite-extension invariance, the Chow identity and (2.4) give hXan(z,w)=hXEan(zE,wE)=∑jhXEan(vj∗uj∗zE,wE)=∑jhAjan(uj∗zE,tvj∗wE).\begin{aligned} h_X^{\mathrm{an}}(z,w) &=h_{X_E}^{\mathrm{an}}(z_E,w_E)\\ &=\sum_jh_{X_E}^{\mathrm{an}}(v_{j*}u_{j*}z_E,w_E)\\ &=\sum_jh_{A_j}^{\mathrm{an}}(u_{j*}z_E,{}^tv_{j*}w_E). \end{aligned}hXan​(z,w)​=hXE​an​(zE​,wE​)=j∑​hXE​an​(vj∗​uj∗​zE​,wE​)=j∑​hAj​an​(uj∗​zE​,tvj∗​wE​).​ The image classes are homologically trivial and have codimensions r+ajr+a_jr+aj​ and dim⁡Aj+1−r−aj\dim A_j+1-r-a_jdimAj​+1−r−aj​. An image in codimension zero is zero because its geometric cycle class detects its rank. Out-of-range images also vanish. Apply (2.5) to each remaining term to obtain (1.7). Every permitted choice computes the same canonical left side, proving independence. This completes the proof of Theorem 1.4.
